inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation' add-back $553m (BMY_Annual_FY2025.txt:4949). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; the financing line 'Stock option proceeds and other, net' is immaterial (-$25m 9M 2026), so the cash-flow add-back is used as the combined figure.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for Q3 2026, 2,053m (BMY_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:2715). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. No repurchases in FY2024, FY2025 or 9M 2026 ($5.0bn authorisation unused), so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding with buybacks; the $5bn/yr dividend is where the cash goes.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q net debt table (BMY_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:3747-3754): cash and equivalents 9,574 + marketable debt securities 3,007 current + 378 non-current = 12,959 against short-term debt 1,028 + long-term debt 41,849 = 42,877; net debt 29,918. The CSV's CashAndEquivalents (9,574) excludes the marketable securities, which is why `cash` here is larger. Net debt fell $4.1bn in 9M 2026 despite a $3.9bn one-off unwind of the rebates-and-discounts accrual (the Eliquis list-price cut moved gross-to-net from accrued rebates to a lower invoice price).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.65 (large-cap pharma, low cyclicality) gives cost of equity ~7.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (A2/A, 2024-25 USD and EUR senior notes), ~3.9% after tax. Capital structure at market: equity ~$128bn, net debt ~$30bn, so ~81/19, giving ~6.8%; rounded to 7.0% and held identical across scenarios so that the patent-cliff risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for BMY (lease liabilities < $1.5bn against $43bn of debt); lease cost stays inside opex/EBITDA and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is nil in 9M 2026 (-$6m in Q3 2025); no deduction made.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Owner EBITDA = revenue less cost of products sold (ex amortisation), SG&A, R&D, and a NORMALISED acquired-IPRD / business-development charge, plus royalty and licensing income, before SBC, depreciation, amortisation of acquired intangibles, interest, investment income, restructuring, litigation, debt-redemption losses, contingent-consideration and equity-investment marks. FY2025 on this basis: pre-tax earnings 9,328 + amortisation 3,317 + depreciation ~694 + interest expense 1,891 - investment income 586 + restructuring 563 + litigation 434 + debt-redemption loss 356 + contingent consideration 351 - equity gains 280 + SBC 553 = ~16.6bn, 34.5% of revenue, AFTER the 3,721 of acquired IPRD charged in 2025. The IPRD/BD charge is deliberately kept inside EBITDA at roughly 6-7% of revenue: reported FCF (OCF - capex) EXCLUDES it because asset-acquisition IPRD is added back in operating cash flow and the cash sits in investing ($3.9bn in FY2025, ~$1.3bn in 9M 2026 plus the $600m Hengrui upfront and a $500m anniversary payment), yet buying the pipeline that replaces the Eliquis/Opdivo revenue is the central recurring cost of this business. 9M 2026 on the same basis ran ~38% with IPRD at only 4.4% of revenue, i.e. ~36% normalised, which is where the FY2026 margin is set.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating pharmaceutical company; routing table row 1). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (December year-end); year 1 = FY2026, of which 9 months are reported. Revenue path is built product-by-product from the FY2025 10-K exclusivity table and the Q3 2026 10-Q product table, not extrapolated from the FY2025/FY2026 totals: FY2026 is a local PEAK, not a base. (1) Eliquis (~$18bn FY2026 run-rate after the US list-price/GTN restructuring lifted 9M revenue 21%) loses EU composition-of-matter protection November 2026 and US exclusivity in 2028 under the generic settlements; small-molecule erosion is modelled to ~$2.5bn by 2031. (2) Opdivo + Opdivo Qvantig (~$10.4bn) lose US exclusivity 2028 and EU 2030; biosimilar erosion to ~$3.5bn by 2035. (3) Revlimid (volume-limited licences ended January 2026, -54% YTD), Pomalyst (US generics March 2026, -59% YTD), Sprycel and Abraxane are already a ~$2.9bn tail falling to ~$0.8bn. (4) The growth portfolio ex-Opdivo (~$19bn FY2026: Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Camzyos, Opdualag, Yervoy, Orencia, Cobenfy, Sotyktu, Krazati, Zeposia, Zenbexus/iberdomide, mezigdomide PDUFA May 2027, arlo-cel, RYZ101, iza-bren, pumitamig/BNT327, admilparant) compounds ~9%/yr in the base case through 2030, then slows as Reblozyl (US 2031), Breyanzi/Opdualag/Sotyktu/Zeposia (2033-34) hit their own exclusivity dates. Total revenue therefore runs ~48.2bn (FY2025) -> ~50.6bn (FY2026) -> ~37.7bn trough (FY2029) -> ~38.5bn (FY2035). Margins step down with the loss of the highest-margin revenue (Eliquis, Opdivo), partly cushioned by the $2bn strategic productivity programme, the end of the Pfizer Eliquis profit share, and the end of the ~$1.1bn/yr divestiture-royalty stream (terminated 31 Dec 2025, already out of 9M 2026). Working-capital capture is set slightly negative (manufacturer: receivables and inventory move with revenue), so the revenue decline releases a little cash. D&A for cash tax is kept at ~2% of revenue (depreciation ~$0.7bn plus a small deductible slice of the $1.8bn amortisation) because the Celgene-era intangible amortisation is largely non-deductible; cash tax rate starts at 18% (FY2025 non-GAAP ETR 18.8%, 9M 2026 GAAP 17.3%, OBBBA R&D expensing) and drifts to 20%. Capex $1.3bn guided for 2026, with the Houston and Whitestown manufacturing builds lifting it to ~$1.3-1.4bn in 2027-2030, which is a rising % of a shrinking revenue base. Terminal cap multiple set at 14x owner FCF (structurally LOE-cycling business; method says 12-15x for such) with 2.0% terminal growth; the cap binds in all three scenarios. The 9M 2026 reported FCF ($7.7bn) is depressed by the one-off $3.9bn rebate-accrual unwind and is NOT the run-rate; underlying unlevered FCF ex-BD annualises ~$16bn, ~$13bn after a normalised $3.3bn BD charge, which is what the year-1 component build produces. Street basis (SBC as non-cash) is only ~1% of revenue here, so the house/street band is narrow. last_fcf = reported_fcf 12,845 - sbc 553 - interest_income 586 = 11,706; it is a levered figure (after ~$1.9bn interest paid) and after no BD cash, so it is an anchor for the reader, not the engine's year-1 flow.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR from the product-level LOE build (FY2025 48.2bn -> FY2035 38.5bn); the historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy because FY2026 is the pre-cliff peak
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-13% to -16%/yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (+1.5% to +2.5%) and EPS: book value was consumed by the $12.1bn Karuna IPRD write-off (FY2024 net loss -$8.9bn), $19bn of buybacks in FY2021-23 and a $5bn/yr dividend exceeding GAAP earnings in several years. EPS 5-year CAGR is undefined (FY2020 EPS -3.99 on the Celgene/MyoKardia IPRD charges). Owner-FCF CAGR (-1.1% 5y, +1.1% 3y) is below reported FCF CAGR (-0.7% 5y, +2.4% 3y) because interest income rose from $121m to $586m on the larger cash pile and SBC was broadly flat; the gap is interest income, not SBC growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5% (9M actual +5.2%, Eliquis +21% on the GTN restructuring, growth portfolio +13%, legacy ex-Eliquis -40%). FY2027 ~flat: Eliquis EU generics from Nov-2026 and the end of the divestiture royalty offset ~8% growth-portfolio gains. FY2028 -12% and FY2029 -15.5%: Eliquis US generics (settlement date 2028) take it from ~17.5bn to ~4.5bn over two years; Opdivo US biosimilars late 2028. FY2030 -4.5%: Opdivo EU 2030. FY2031-35 +0.5% to +2%: pipeline launches (Cobenfy, mezigdomide, arlo-cel, iza-bren, pumitamig, RYZ101, admilparant) roughly offset the Reblozyl 2031 and Breyanzi/Opdualag/Sotyktu/Zeposia 2033-34 exclusivity losses.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 owner EBITDA 34.5% after 3.7bn IPRD. FY2026 36.5%: 9M actual ~38% with light IPRD, normalised to ~6.5% BD spend, plus productivity savings and the Eliquis net-price lift. Steps down to 29% at the FY2030 trough as the two highest-margin franchises erode faster than opex, then recovers to 31% as the growth portfolio scales and the Pfizer Eliquis profit share (in COGS) disappears with Eliquis itself.

bull.growth_rationale: Same LOE dates, slower erosion and a stronger replacement engine: Eliquis US generic ramp is gradual (settlement entrants only, no at-risk launches), Opdivo Qvantig conversion and slow biosimilar uptake hold the nivolumab franchise at ~60% of peak through 2030, and the growth portfolio ex-Opdivo compounds ~12%/yr with Cobenfy reaching $4bn+, iza-bren and pumitamig becoming multi-billion oncology franchises, and mezigdomide/arlo-cel/Zenbexus rebuilding the myeloma franchise. Revenue troughs at ~44bn in FY2029 and is back above 55bn by FY2035.

bear.growth_rationale: The cliff on schedule with the replacement engine under-delivering: Eliquis EU and pricing pressure already bite in FY2027, US generics erode Eliquis to <$3bn by 2030, nivolumab biosimilars take Opdivo to ~$3bn by 2031, Cobenfy stays a ~$1bn schizophrenia drug after the adjunctive/Alzheimer's programmes disappoint, one or more of the late-stage oncology bets (iza-bren, pumitamig) fails to differentiate in the US, and Orencia's 2028 IRA price applies. Revenue troughs near 30bn and only crawls thereafter, while BD spend has to rise to refill the pipeline, holding margins at ~26%.

scenario_narratives.base: BMY is a company whose FY2026 revenue (~$50.6bn) and FCF are a local peak, not a base. Two franchises worth ~$28bn of revenue, Eliquis and Opdivo, lose exclusivity in 2028 (EU Eliquis November 2026, EU Opdivo 2030), on top of Revlimid and Pomalyst, which have already collapsed in 2026. The base case takes the FY2025 10-K exclusivity table at face value, erodes Eliquis as a small molecule (fast) and Opdivo as a biologic (slower), and lets the growth portfolio ex-Opdivo compound ~9%/yr to a ~$28bn franchise by 2031 before its own 2031-34 exclusivity dates slow it. Revenue troughs at ~$37.7bn in FY2029 and is ~$38.5bn in FY2035; owner-EBITDA margin troughs at 29% and settles at 31%. Business development is treated as a recurring ~6.5%-of-revenue cost inside EBITDA because reported FCF excludes it and BMY cannot replace $25bn of LOE revenue without buying pipeline. On these flows the $5bn/yr dividend is covered through the trough, but not by much in FY2029-30.
scenario_narratives.bull: The replacement engine works and erosion is slower than the calendar implies: Eliquis settles into a gradual multi-year US generic ramp, Opdivo Qvantig retains a large share of the nivolumab franchise, Cobenfy becomes a $4bn+ psychiatry franchise, and the 2025-26 oncology deals (iza-bren with SystImmune, pumitamig/BNT327 with BioNTech) plus RYZ101, mezigdomide, arlo-cel and Zenbexus produce several multi-billion launches by 2030. Revenue troughs at ~$44bn and is back to ~$55bn by FY2035 with 35% margins. Even here the cap multiple binds, so the upside is mostly from the flows, not the exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cliff on schedule and the pipeline under-delivering: Eliquis EU generics and US pricing pressure hit from FY2027, US generics erode Eliquis below $3bn by 2030, nivolumab biosimilars take Opdivo to ~$3bn by 2031, Cobenfy stays a ~$1bn drug, one of the big oncology bets fails to differentiate in the US, and Orencia's 2028 IRA price applies. Revenue troughs near $30bn; margins fall to 25-26% because BD spend has to rise to refill the pipeline. The $5bn/yr dividend would then exceed owner FCF in FY2029-30 and the balance sheet (~$30bn net debt, $8.9bn maturing through 2030) would force a dividend cut or more leverage.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 30/50/20. The LOE calendar is contractual and public, so the question is only how fast erosion runs and whether the pipeline refills the hole: the bull case needs several independent clinical and commercial outcomes to go right at once (Cobenfy beyond schizophrenia, two 2025-26 licensed oncology assets differentiating in the US, slow nivolumab biosimilar uptake), which argues for a lower bull weight; the bear case is simply the cliff as scheduled with a pipeline that performs like the sector average, which is at least a 30% outcome. There is no going-concern risk (A-rated, no covenants), so bear is not taken higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value BMY as a run-off of two giant franchises plus an option on the replacement portfolio, not as a compounding pharma. Each product is eroded from its own exclusivity date, business development is charged as a recurring cost, and the terminal multiple is capped at 14x because the growth portfolio itself faces a second exclusivity wave in 2031-34. The sanity-check concern that a model might extrapolate FY2026 cash flow (Eliquis +21%, record margins) is addressed structurally: the base case has revenue 25% below FY2026 by FY2029 and never regains it within the horizon.
key_risks_to_valuation: Eliquis US generic timing and ramp (settlement date 2028; an at-risk launch or a faster ramp moves FY2028-29 flows materially; the October 2026 infringement action shows new challengers are filing)
Opdivo biosimilar uptake in the US from 2028 and the Opdivo Qvantig conversion rate

Pipeline conversion of the 2024-26 deal spree (Karuna/Cobenfy, SystImmune/iza-bren, BioNTech/pumitamig, RayzeBio/RYZ101, Hengrui) into multi-billion franchises by 2030; the bull/bear spread is almost entirely this
IRA: Pomalyst MFP from 2027, Orencia from 2028, and the risk that further growth-portfolio products are selected
Normalised business-development spend: the model charges ~6.5% of revenue; FY2024 spent $22bn on Karuna, RayzeBio and Mirati and another large acquisition would be a further drain on owner FCF
Dividend sustainability through the FY2029-30 trough on ~$30bn of net debt; a cut is a scenario, not a valuation input, but it is where the bear case lands
Terminal assumptions: a 14x cap on year-10 owner FCF binds in every scenario, so the valuation is sensitive to that cap and to the FY2035 margin rather than to terminal growth
